claims.text: At high temperatures, FeNiCrCoCu coating wear resistance is governed by formation of an oxide tribolayer.
The governing tribolayer is adherent and finely dispersed.
The oxide tribolayer is enriched in Cr and Cu.
The oxide tribolayer mitigates localized stresses and microcracking.
The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating on a conventional metal substrate with no engineered oxide scale.
A controlled pre-oxidation treatment at approximately 500°C for 1 hour under low oxygen partial pressure is the proposed intervention.
Pre-oxidation produces a continuous, ultra-thin oxide scale consisting primarily of Cr oxides and Cu oxides.
The pre-formed oxide scale adheres well to the underlying FeNiCrCoCu alloy and remains intact during wear.
Selective oxidation of Cr and Cu at elevated temperatures forms the protective tribolayer.
The protective tribolayer distributes contact stresses.
Reduced friction and distributed contact stresses minimize dislocation pile-up and microcrack nucleation at grain boundaries during sliding.
Minimizing dislocation pile-up and grain-boundary microcrack nucleation enhances wear resistance.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated as-deposited coatings during high-temperature wear testing.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have a wear rate approximately 20–30% lower than untreated as-deposited coatings during high-temperature wear testing.
Untreated coatings are expected to exhibit higher friction and accelerated wear because they lack an engineered protective oxide scale.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate between 500°C and 700°C under moderate loading in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
Substantially lower temperatures may not activate protective oxide formation.
Extremely high loads may overwhelm the protective oxide layer.
